description:
Found while writing the float-rendering oracle fixture for fz-5xp.15.

    fn main(), do: dbg(1.0e14)

  error[parse/expected-token]: expected `)`, got Ident("e14")

Every spelling fails, on all three doors, because the lexer ends the number at
`1.0` and hands `e14` on as an identifier:

    1.0e14   -> Ident("e14")
    1.0e-7   -> Ident("e")
    1e10     -> Ident("e10")
    1.5E3    -> Upper("E3")

Elixir accepts all of these (`1.0e14`, `1.0e-7`, `1_000.5e-3`), and they are
ordinary Elixir source, so this is a surface-parity gap rather than a missing
feature.

WHY IT MATTERS NOW. A float outside roughly 1e-4 .. 1e16 CANNOT BE WRITTEN in
fz source at all. `behavior/float_rendering` therefore cannot cover the values
whose rendering is most interesting -- `1.0e-7`, `1.7976931348623157e308`,
`5.0e-324` -- and those are exactly the ones where the two notations trade
places. They are pinned in the runtime's unit tests by BIT PATTERN instead,
which works but cannot be exercised through the doors.

fz-5xp.17's JSON decoder must also accept exponents in its INPUT
(`{"x": 1.0e-7}` is valid JSON), and that is a separate scanner. But a decoder
whose own test data cannot be written as fz literals is awkward to build, and
`Json.encode` will emit exponents that fz source cannot then read back.

DONE = `1.0e14`, `1e10`, `1.0e-7` and `1.5E3` lex as float literals and agree on
all three doors, with the fixture above extended to the values it currently has
to omit. Check the underscore separator (`1_000.5`) while in there, since
Elixir allows it and it is the same lexer state.
title: [BUG] Float literals cannot have an exponent
